answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge admission through a kernel of staked reputation: each new agent locks a small bond before it may join a work grove, and peers slash that bond when its output is copied or fake. A bond alone is cheap to forge at scale, so entry also demands a quartz-hard proof of unique compute, a verifiable workload tied to one hardware key per agent. Identities sharing a key, funding trail, or identical outputs are merged and their bonds burned together, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds and proofs, while one honest agent pays once.
